# Representative values consistent with the NIST Chemistry WebBook isothermal properties
# for CO2 at 280 K. Hand-constructed for this course from published literature figures for
# CO2's critical point and its 280 K saturation curve -- this is not a live pull from NIST's
# database (this machine has no network access to query it)
# of the real shape and scale of the isotherm rather than a digit-for-digit NIST export.
# Reference values used to build this table (NIST Chemistry WebBook
#   P_sat(280 K) = 4.1663e6 Pa                            (saturation / vapour pressure)
#   rho_vapour
#   rho_liquid
#   M(CO2) = 44.01e-3 kg/mol
# Columns: temperature_K
#   Rows 1-8   -- dilute-to-near-saturated CO2 vapour (isothermal compression at 280 K).
#   Rows 8-14  -- the 280 K condensation plateau: 280 K is below CO2's T_c = 304.13 K
#                 real substance holds P = P_sat exactly constant while V drops through the
#                 two-phase (liquid + vapour) region -- the flat segment a real gas follows
#                 in contrast to the unphysical van der Waals loop over the same volume range.
#   Rows 14-16 -- the compressed-liquid branch just past the plateau
#                 all liquid and pressure rises steeply for a small further reduction in V.
